The login protection of 2026-10-01 (SEC.1, SEC.20 to
SEC.28: the always-on activity log, per-address and per-username
lockouts, trusted devices, the password blocklist and hashing cost,
two-factor sign-in and the fail2ban example) shipped in PRs #217, #220
and #221.

Design: [docs/design/operations/login-brute-force-protection.md](design/operations/login-brute-force-protection.md)

- [ ] **SEC.33 Release gate: a full security code audit of the whole code base, done before every major or minor version change (8.1 first)**
  Boss, 2026-10-21, 5:10 PM EDT: before 8.1 is stamped finished there
  must be a full security code audit, and it MUST be done before every
  single major or minor version change (8.1, 8.2 and on to 9.0 and 10.0;
  the 8.0.NNNN builds are exempt). One standing item: it stays open and
  is re-run for each major or minor version change, never retired.
  Confirmed and narrowed to this wording by Boss, 8:01 PM EDT
  2026-10-22: required whenever the major or minor number changes, not
  for build numbers. Scope: every route, API
  endpoint and form; sign-in, sessions, cookies, CSRF, rate limits and
  lockouts; authorization and every admin page; all SQL and any string
  built into a query; file, path and upload handling and the tile cache
  and jobs directory; the stored-XSS and output-escaping paths in
  templates and JavaScript; the Content-Security-Policy and headers;
  secrets, config and settings handling; the dependency list and its
  known vulnerabilities (pip and npm lockfiles); the install, update and
  deployment scripts and the systemd and Apache or nginx examples; the
  Redis and job-queue inputs; and anything new since the last pass (use
  git log since the last audited release). Run the repository's own
  static checks and add a scanner pass where one can run without the
  network. Done: for the release, a dated report
  (/mnt/project-files/reports/release-audit-security-<version>.md,
  linked from the goal issue and logged on this item as 'Release log:
  <version>, <EDT date and time>, <commit>') that names the commit
  audited, lists what was covered and what was not, and files every
  finding as its own item (a high or critical finding blocks the release
  until fixed and merged; the rest are filed with an owner). The release
  is not stamped while the report for its version is missing, or while a
  finding it marks blocking is open. Proposed owner: its own thread,
  started when the version nears close (8.1: after the whole-sphere
  audits TEST.185, TEST.184, TEST.159 and TEST.160 merge, so the audit
  sees the final code); it must not be the lane that wrote the code
  under audit.
  Ordering (TODO thread, 6:40 PM EDT 2026-10-21): this audit runs after
  the performance profile PERF.146 so it sees the final code.
  Owner: a new audit thread, started when PERF.146 closes (Boss, 7:44
  PM EDT 2026-10-22: all five cores on 8.1; this replaces any earlier
  owner line).
  Method: follow /mnt/project-files/reports/audit-playbook-2026-10-22.md
  (the coordinator, relayed 7:58 PM EDT 2026-10-22 as the lane's clock
  reads).
  Gate rule (Boss, 8:04 PM EDT 2026-10-22): the
  version is not stamped while a confirmed Critical or High finding is
  open; Mediums are filed with owners; data loss, corruption or broken
  seed reproducibility counts as High. This holds unless Boss
  specifically authorizes an exception.
  Prerequisites: none. Related: TEST.261.
  Release log: 8.1 first pass, 6:00 PM EST on 2026-11-06, d371f13e1 (report /mnt/project-files/reports/release-audit-security-8.1.md, verdict PASS WITH FILED ITEMS, no Critical or High; findings filed as SEC.37 to SEC.42; the delta pass runs at the end of 8.1).

- [ ] **PERF.254 Memory governor for the generation run: admit and shed workers from the live free memory, learn each stage's worker size, and measure the cut of a stage as its own step**
  Lane 22's write-up: /mnt/project-files/reports/memory-kills-and-dynamic-workers-2026-11-08.md; library research: /mnt/project-files/reports/job-library-research-2026-11-08.md (15 libraries read; none re-reads the host while a run goes); Lane 22's Dask assessment: /mnt/project-files/reports/perf254-dask-assessment-2026-11-08.md. Boss chose option 1 of the research (3:34 PM EST on 2026-11-08, 'Send to todo to build option 1'): keep RQ 2.12.0 (no upgrade to RQ 3.0 in this item) and build our own weighted memory gate in Redis fed by psutil. Dask is dropped as the lead (OPS.125 is dropped unless Boss revives it); a Ray one-stage spike is optional and only if Boss asks. Today every worker size is a number measured once in queue/workers.py (STAGE_WORKER_MEMORY_MB) and nothing reads the host while a run goes. Do: add psutil 7.2.2 (new dependency: requirements.lock and the setup script through update.sh); every job carries a claim_mb; a job starts only when the running claims plus its claim plus a reserve fit the budget taken from MemAvailable, re-read every 5 seconds, with a bounded wait and a fallback to the table cap so a wrong gate cannot stall a run; a log line for every decision; claims start from the table and rise to the largest peak seen (units.peak_resident_mb); a job killed for memory retries once with a larger claim, then the run stops with the job named (the idea comes from Snakemake); the cut of a stage into units runs as a claimed job that reads counts per sky cell (GROUP BY), not rows; scale the figures with galaxy size. The job-model fields (claim, dependencies, subjobs) belong to OPS.122 and OPS.124 and the design thread that owns them; this item builds the gate on today's queue, and OPS.124 carries it onto the job model. Output must stay byte-identical (the work seed does not depend on the worker count). Scope (Boss, 3:34 PM EST on 2026-11-08: 'All jobs operate under dynamic load and memory limits to not overload and kill the machine ALLLLLL JOBS'): the gate covers ALL jobs of every kind, with no exempt type: every RQ queue and lane (bulk stage units, scatters, warm-ups, interactive, long and maintenance lanes, API and page jobs, admin tasks, imports, tests and gates, maps, the cut of a stage, anything the web app starts); one gate and one budget; a claim for every job kind (a default claim for a kind with no measured figure, learned from observed peaks); admission also reads the CPU load, not only MemAvailable, so ordinary workers stay under the host cap; the places reserved for interactive work still hold; a test fails when any job kind has no claim, so nothing slips past the gate. Fair-share rule (Boss, 3:44 PM EST on 2026-11-08: 'we want to use a task scheduler and sharing system time so warmup or other commands do not block the site so all tasks that can run get a chance to run'): jobs are scheduled by a task scheduler that shares system time fairly: fair share across job kinds, priority for work that serves the site, no starvation (aging raises a waiting job's turn), and no command, the warm-up included, can block the site; OPS.130 builds the scheduler. Needs Lane 13's measurement of what the cut holds. Done: a full galaxy run on a 16 GB host finishes past stage 13 with no kernel kill, a job killed for memory is retried once and then named, every job kind has a claim (test), and a run with all lanes busy keeps the host under its cap. Lock-free, queue code only; Boss's order: first, before GEN.1441.
  Built (Lane 22, PR 5760, merged 2026-11-08): the gate. Leftovers settled (Lane 22, 2026-11-08): the sky-cell GROUP BY is closed without a build, because PERF.252 (PR 5727) already limits the backfill to charted sectors (a galaxy now opens on 23 sectors and 7 sky cells) and the sky units depend only on the set of 50 pc cells, so a count query would save a few MB and risk changing which cells are planned. Left: the 16 GB full-galaxy run past stage 13, which no code settles; it happens on Boss's test server at his next full run, and the gate's wait lines and the kill report show any shortfall. Retire this item when that run passes.

- [ ] **GEN.1587 (bug) The class is judged before the latitude bands exist, so M, O, H, P and R never match at build: FORCE_CLASS M is unmet on 10 of 10 seeds and every slot request wastes its draws (the moon class is also applied before its water is remade)**
  Bug sweep by reading and simulating the generator (first batch, coordinator relay 2026-11-12), reports/bug-sweep-read-and-simulate-2026-11-11.md, H3 and M1, confirmed by run. generation/planet.py lines 474-476 and 506-508, physics/planets.py lines 356-362 and 527-529 and generation/validation.py lines 183-195 apply the class, then make motion, spin and habitability_world.generate (the only place the bands are made); the classes that read the hottest and coldest region, the night side and the wet bulb (class_domains.derived) see None and score 0. An Earth twin without bands is F at match 0.0, with bands M at 1.0. StarSystem.build_planet (system.py lines 1989-2006) compares each fresh draw with the class asked for, so for M, O, H, P or R every draw is thrown away, the last is kept and _request_unreachable is set (FORCE_CLASS M unmet on all 10 seeds 0 to 9; FORCE_CLASS K met on 2 of 3); the system retry at system.py lines 438 and 480 judges forced classes on the same early class; a body remade at its final age is classed with old bands. The stored class of a finished planet is put right by _finish_planet (system.py line 2209), so finished labels are right; requests and slots are broken. Second part (M1): _finish_planet applies each moon's class (system.py lines 2211-2212) before _finish_moon (lines 2216-2219) runs refresh_at_final_age, which remakes hydrosphere, aquifer and groundwater; the class is applied again only if life changed the air. Do: make the bands (or whatever the band-reading classes need) before any class that judges a request, and apply the moon class after its water is remade, reusing habitability_world.generate and the existing class code (no second class pass). GEN.1548 (reorder, class and life last) removes the same ordering for the main build once built; this item is the fix for the request path and the retries and may fold into GEN.1548 if Lane 05 reaches it first (confirm with TODO; do not build the same thing twice). Done: a test that FORCE_CLASS M is met on a seeded system that can make an M (and O, H, P, R), the Earth-twin case, the moon case, before and after class counts on scripts/class_census.py. Bears directly on the class M yield. Lock item (changes output, new epoch).
  Priority (coordinator, 2026-11-12): does not change the Earth analog numbers, but blocks habitable-world and FORCE_CLASS requests from ever seeing an M, so it is high in the M fix order (with GEN.1581, GEN.1584). Split agreed 2026-11-12: Lane 14 builds the band-before-class piece and the force-class judgment first; Lane 05 builds the GEN.1548 reorder around it.

- [ ] **GEN.1588 (bug) The greenhouse table gives huge temperature swings for trace gases (1 Pa HCN adds 76 K, 0.001 Pa of ozone, N2O or ethane adds 10 K, 1 Pa helium adds 75 K, 0.1 Pa ammonia or hydrogen removes the greenhouse): refit or cut off each gas below the share the fit has data for**
  Bug sweep by reading and simulating the generator (first batch, coordinator relay 2026-11-12), reports/bug-sweep-read-and-simulate-2026-11-11.md, H1, confirmed by run. physics/greenhouse_table.py lines 127-152 (features, log_ratio) and physics/data/greenhouse_table.json take ln(share + 1e-9) for each gas; the fit saw each gas either absent or at a real share, so between 1e-9 and about 1e-4 it invents a slope. On Earth's air (table answer 286.1 K): HCN 281.0, 297.4, 361.8 and 717.8 K at 0.001, 0.1, 1 and 100 Pa; any 'other infrared' gas (C2H4, C2H6, O3, N2O) 295.8, 311.5, 318.7 and 343.7 K; SO2 294.9 to 390.9 K; NH3 276.8, 256.5, 255.0, 271.5 K; H2 282.4 down to 255.0 K; helium (no infrared at all) 298.2 to 383.4 K; CH4 is fine (286.0 to 290.4 K). ln_fraction_weak has scale 1e-9 and equal low and high bounds, so 'weak' gases never count. Seed 131: a 293 K ocean world, after life burned its CO to CO2, was stored at 562 K; without its 0.033 Pa of HCN the same table gives 343 K. Over 80 systems (233 bodies with air) the table moves by more than 5 K for 117 bodies, 20 K for 80 and 50 K for 54 when gases under 1e-4 are left out (mostly PH3, HCl, NH3, CO, NO, Ar). Trap: trace_air.apply adds N2O, PH3, NO2 and CH3Cl after the temperature is solved and says it does not move; true only while nothing re-solves it. Do: either refit with samples that cover trace shares for every gas, or apply each gas only above the share where the fit has data and scale its effect to zero below it (as is done for thin air and noble-gas airs); reuse the fitting script and the existing cutoff pattern; register any cutoff as a stand-in in GEN.725. The temperature of the worlds nearest class M is the least reliable until this lands. Done: the table above re-run (each gas at 0.001, 0.1, 1 and 100 Pa moves by a physically small amount), the 80-system sample before and after, class counts before and after, tests. Lock item (changes output, new epoch).

- [ ] **GEN.1591 (bug) The lid regime and surface temperature the air solve reads are left over from the previous pass: a remade body is solved under the earlier regime, and generate_lid redraws the regime on each remake so a world can flip regime after its air was solved**
  Bug sweep by reading and simulating the generator (first batch, coordinator relay 2026-11-12), reports/bug-sweep-read-and-simulate-2026-11-11.md, M0 (read only, not yet run). physics/planets.py line 666 calls interior_heat.update_heat, which reads lid_of(body) (interior_heat.py lines 593-596) and surface_of(body) (lines 615-618). On the first build lid_regime and surface_temperature are unset, so the solve uses a stagnant lid and a default surface (intended, per the lid_of docstring); after the solve generate_lid (lines 621-633) draws the real regime. On any remake (final age, moved orbit, late accretion) the solve uses the regime and temperature of the pass before, lid_regime is never cleared in generate_planet_properties, and generate_lid draws again. Result: outgassing and the CO2 supply depend on how often a body was remade, and the stored lid can disagree with the lid the stored air was solved under; a plate-tectonic world never remade has the air of a stagnant-lid world. Do: confirm by run, then key the lid draw to the body (GEN.1547) and make a remake follow the same rule as the first build, or iterate the lid and the air to one answer; reuse generate_lid and update_heat. Done: a test that the stored lid is the lid the stored air was solved under, on a remade and a never-remade body, before and after counts of lid regimes. Lock item (changes output, new epoch).

- [ ] **GEN.1611 (bug) The formation snow line follows the star's present brightness: white dwarfs get 0.02 to 0.2 au and giants 13 to 22 au, so ice shares, giant ices, belt type and origins and the disk edge are wrong around evolved stars; and the snow-line scatter allows a factor of 4, putting it inside the habitable zone for 104 of 3,000 stars**
  Bug sweep fourth batch (coordinator relay 2026-11-12; Boss: fix all sweep findings in 8.1, 'Build it and Ship it'), reports/bug-sweep-read-and-simulate-2026-11-11.md section 'Fourth batch', M9, confirmed by run. generation/star.py lines 346-347 call formation.draw_snow_line_au(self.luminosity, ...) with today's luminosity; generation/belt_birth.py lines 115-117 pass the same value as both present and formation snow line and scale the disk's outer edge from it. From 3,000 drawn stars: a white dwarf born at 4.36 solar masses (0.00005 Sun today) stores 0.02 au, one born at 1.43 (0.0001 Sun) 0.03 au; K4III and K3III giants born at 1.04 and 1.73 solar masses store 21.8 and 13.5 au. Everything that asks 'made beyond the ice line' reads it: ice shares of planets and moons, a giant's ices, icy or rocky belts, belt origins, the disk edge. White dwarfs are 7.5 percent of drawn stars, giants and subgiants about 0.4 percent. Second part: SNOW_LINE_SCATTER_MAX_SIGMA 3.0 x 0.2 dex allows a factor of 4 either way (the docstring says the real spread is 2 to 3), so for 104 of 3,000 stars (mostly M and K dwarfs) the drawn snow line lies inside the inner habitable-zone edge. Do: draw the formation snow line from the star's birth (pre-main-sequence or zero-age) luminosity for its initial mass (reuse the stellar-state tables), store it apart from the present snow line where both are read, and pass the formation one to belt_birth and every 'formed beyond' test; bring the scatter cap to the sourced spread (cite as [R....] ids, register in GEN.725). Done: a test that a white dwarf and a giant get the snow line of their progenitor's birth, the scatter test against the sourced spread, before and after counts of icy planets, belts and disk edges around evolved stars. ## USR: User accounts

- [ ] **USR.1 User accounts**
  Boss (2026-10-01): "a full user level interface to allow users to
  bookmark this will, of course, require an email loop for password
  setting / resetting, invite only, so only an admin can invite a user
  which is done by unique link". Today there are only admin accounts:
  `admin_users`, `admin_sessions`, `admin_api_keys` and
  `admin_audit_log` in `stellarObjects/control_schema.sql`, managed by
  `stellarObjects/adminAuth.py`. Install seeds one admin with a random
  first password and `must_change_credentials`
  (`bootstrap_control_schema`), and nothing in the web interface or the
  CLI adds another account. There is no email support and no
  saved-bookmark feature (pages only have bookmarkable URLs). Order:
  USR.2, then USR.3 and USR.4, then USR.5, USR.6 and USR.7.
  Login protection already exists per username
  (`src/html/api/loginbackoff.py`, PR #131) and is planned per IP
  address (SEC.1); both must cover user logins, password resets and
  invite links too, as must SEC.20's logging and SEC.26's second
  factor.
  Research (2026-10-09, settings-seo-and-accounts.md): order stays; add
  one shared table `account_tokens` used by USR.4, USR.5 and USR.6
  (itsdangerous is not used for these tokens). The text names stale
  paths (`stellarObjects/control_schema.sql`,
  `stellarObjects/adminAuth.py`, `src/html/api/loginbackoff.py`); the
  files are now `src/planetgen/db/control_schema.sql`,
  `src/planetgen/admin/auth.py` and `src/planetgen/admin/throttle.py`
  with `api/loginguard.py`.

  Headline: 8.2 (user accounts, with sign-up by an email invitation that
  only an admin can send).
  - [ ] **USR.2 Accounts with roles: user, moderator, admin and Owner**
    Boss: "Admin can
    then make a user admin or take away admin rights on everything but the
    primary 1st admin account generated at install, that'll have a
    designation of 'Owner' and no other account can override that." Done:
    one accounts table in the control database (with an email address)
    holding a role per account (user, moderator, admin, Owner; moderator
    is stored and valid from the start, has no permissions until 10.0
    and no page assigns it, Boss 2026-10-16, 1:43 PM EDT); exactly one
    Owner,
    which is the account install creates; an admin page where admins
    promote a user to admin or demote an admin to user, refused for the
    Owner; sessions and API keys that work for every role while the
    admin-only pages and API routes stay admin-only; each role change
    written to the audit log. Question (decided below): does
    `admin_users` become
    this table (renamed, with a role column) or do users get their own
    table? Which existing account becomes Owner on a server that already
    has several admins (the lowest id?)? Can an admin demote themselves,
    or another admin? Can an admin delete or disable a user account? Do
    users get API keys?
    Research (2026-10-09, settings-seo-and-accounts.md): answer the open
    questions as in B7: one table with a role column (renamed to
    `accounts` in a follow-up; open question for Boss, default: add
    columns now); the lowest id becomes Owner; a database-level
    single-Owner unique index on a generated column; admins cannot
    demote themselves; admins disable users, only the Owner disables
    admins; delete by self or Owner; admins create API keys only at
    first. Add the console CLI `planetgen.cli.accounts
    --set-owner/--reset-password`. The control schema is the next
    Alembic revision after the current one.
    Decided (2026-10-10): Boss (19:16Z, Accept all): one accounts table
    with a role column (add the columns now, rename later); the lowest
    id is the Owner.
    Roles must fit 10.0 (roles and permissions, USR.25) without a
    rebuild: the role is one text column holding one of the four values;
    every admin-only page, route and command goes through one guard
    (`require_role`) so 10.0 swaps that single function for the
    permission check `can()` (USR.12, USR.14); no code outside that
    guard compares a role; the role change page of this item writes the
    audit row through one function that 10.0 reuses for the moderator
    role (USR.13).
    Split (2026-10-16, Boss 1:07 PM EDT: look at each item for smaller
    chunks and shared work): this item is now the umbrella and is done
    when its subitems are: DB.58, USR.26, USR.27. It mixes a
    control-database migration (role, email, status, single-Owner index
    and, per the later flows, the shared token and invite tables), the
    role model in sessions, API keys and guards (which USR.3, USR.4,
    USR.5, USR.7, USR.8 and API.6 actually wait for), an admin page and
    a console CLI.
  Decided (Boss, contradiction sweep cards, taps 6:10 to 6:12 PM EDT
  2026-10-18, as the coordinator reported them): fork 9: ADM.86 stays in
  8.1 on the Owner account stub USR.31; the full accounts of this item
  replace the stub in 8.2.

## OPS: Installers, hosting, CI, releases

OPS.1 shipped with the version scheme in `changes/README.md`.

- [ ] **OPS.55 Nightly full backup: a backup step in the daily maintenance run that takes every part into one archive, with a schedule setting and a nightly retention setting**
  Boss (2026-10-16, 2:06 PM EDT): "Yes plese." to a nightly full backup
  from the daily maintenance run. Target 8.9 (the backups and repair
  chain, umbrella ADM.91). The maintenance logic of OPS.16 (`--if-due`,
  `--only STEP`, lock, log, exit codes) gets a `backup` step that calls
  `planetgen.backup.take` of ADM.87 with every registered part
  (settings, control database ADM.88, parity data DB.40), so archives
  are taken without a click. The archive manifest carries a kind
  (`manual`, `settings-save`, `nightly`). The step is due when no
  nightly archive exists for the local day and the local hour has
  reached `settings.nightly_backup_hour` (0 to 23, default 4; the
  scheduler may call the script hourly), and it is switched off by
  `settings.nightly_backup` (default on). Nightly archives are pruned by
  their own count, `settings.nightly_backups_kept` (1 to 60, default 7),
  while `settings.backups_kept` (default 20, 1 to 200) keeps counting
  manual and settings-save archives, so a week of nightly archives never
  pushes out the archive an admin took by hand; the newest archive
  holding every part is never pruned. A failed step logs, exits non-zero
  like any other step and leaves the earlier archives alone; a run that
  finds the guard on (maintenance, an update, a run) skips and is
  retried when next due. The options go into the ADM.42 model and show
  on the settings page. Done: the step with tests for due and not due,
  off, a failure that leaves archives alone, pruning by kind, and a
  second run started during the first exiting at once; the daily run
  lists the step in its log.
  Prerequisites: ADM.88. Related: OPS.16, ADM.87,
  ADM.91.

- [ ] **OPS.64 The version code carries the database schema, generator epoch and API versions as well**
  Asked for by Boss for 8.2. Today the version
  is MAJOR.REVISION.BUILD (for example 8.0.2040) and says nothing about
  which database schema, which generator epoch or which API version a
  build carries, so a database, a generated galaxy or a client cannot be
  matched to a release by its version alone. Make the version code carry
  all three: the database schema version (the Alembic head,
  SCHEMA_VERSION in db/store.py), the generator epoch
  (src/tests/golden/epochs.json) and the API version (API_VERSION in
  api/version.py). Decided (Boss, 12:39 AM EDT 2026-10-24, card option 1, the format is the PEP 440 local suffix): the one version string gains a PEP 440 local
  suffix that the stamping step writes, for example
  8.2.2100+db134.gen62.api5; the three numbers are read from their own
  sources at stamp time, never typed. This touches the version scheme:
  nobody hand-bumps anything, the change goes through
  scripts/bump_version.py (its stamping and its BUILD rule, where BUILD
  stays the count of stamped releases and still never resets),
  _version.py, the README badge and the CHANGELOG entry together, and
  the PR check (--check-pr) must refuse a note or file that sets the
  suffix by hand. setup.py reads __version__ by regex, so the suffix
  must stay a valid package version, and the user agent
  (util/user_agent.py) and every page or response that shows the version
  show the full code. Do:
  choose the format with Boss, teach bump_version.py to build the suffix
  from the three sources, keep its tests and --check-pr in step, and
  update changes/README.md, docs/design/architecture/design-decisions.md (the OPS.1
  version section) and the docs that quote the version format. Done: a
  stamped release carries the three numbers in its version code, they
  match the schema head, the epoch and the API version of that tree, a
  PR that edits the suffix by hand is refused, and the docs gate and the
  bump_version tests pass. Owner: none yet (pool, 8.2). Source: Boss,
  5:07 PM EDT 2026-10-23.
  Prerequisites: none. Related: OPS.56, OPS.1.

- [ ] **POP.29 Design: the world population simulation from habitability scores and the trade routes between spaceports (partner selection, hop runs, the global route list, the map filters, the nearest-route query)**
  Boss, 9:38 PM EDT 2026-10-24 (relayed by the coordinator): "I want you
  to put in a tree by 8.9 to have the system build trade routes, space
  lanes between the largest civilizations. That means we're also going
  to have to have population simulations based on habitability scores so
  To Do needs to build that into the workflow. Start no lower than 8.2
  with a target destination of being done by 8.9 so that by 9.1 we can
  make the trade routes dynamic. The trade routes should use the
  existing pathfinding navigation systems where they will do hop-based
  runs. As in you will set up and generate routes between civilizations
  with a high enough tech level to have spaceports. Between those
  spaceports those will be saved in a global trade route list, which
  will be accessible from all user accounts. It will also have to have a
  filter to see on the star map the paths in question. The filter will
  also need to be able to have the user select an object in the star map
  and then view trade routes going away from that object. It will also
  need to be able to find the nearest trade route either by spaceport
  or, surely, by where they could put themselves in the path of a trade
  route." Write docs/design/habitability/trade-routes.md with its
  sources and stand-in tiers. It decides: (1) the population simulation:
  a world's population is a logistic growth toward a carrying capacity
  set by the habitability scores (Suitability, the food score from Flora
  and Fauna, the land area), the tech band and the civilization's age,
  one closed form per world with a seeded noise draw, so a later dynamic
  version (9.2) can step it in time; (2) which civilizations trade:
  spaceport owners only (POP.21, tech from the settlements design), the
  largest by population first; (3) the partner rule (a gravity model:
  demand rises with the two populations and falls with distance, a cap
  on routes per port, hubs); (4) the hop run: each route is a hop-by-hop
  run on the existing navigation graph (galaxy/nav_graph.py,
  `nav_course` route mode) with a hop length limit from the tech band,
  and what a route stores (the endpoints, the hop list of systems, the
  length in light-years, the hop count, the travel time at the owner's
  tech); (5) the global trade route list: one list for the whole galaxy,
  readable from every account (not per account), changed only by
  generation and by admin editing; (6) the map filter, the routes
  leaving a selected object, and the nearest-route query (nearest
  spaceport with routes, and the nearest point on any route's path where
  someone could put themselves in the way: the nearest system on a hop
  path and the nearest point on a hop segment); (7) what is fixed until
  9.2 makes it dynamic. Done: the design is in the docs with its sources
  and its stand-in list, and every later item of the tree cites it.
  Owner: a research thread with Lane 12 for the map parts. Version 8.2,
  phase 3. Rules: draws through draw.py (GEN.774 streams); a PR that
  changes drawn output carries `tests.golden_update --reason ...
  --affects population` and the next epoch; every number has a unit or
  scale (GEN.772) and a column_units entry; stand-ins get GEN.725
  registry rows with tier and tweak labels; a new command follows the
  PERF.120 rules (one command does one thing); tests are
  `scripts/test.py changed --resume`; no fixed content from the Milky
  Way or the Solar System. Part of the trade tree: POP.29 to POP.36, DB.105, MAP.309, MAP.310, NAV.63, TEST.382.
  Prerequisites: POP.16. Related: POP.16, POP.21, GEN.725, NAV.5.
